A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CQ-DINO and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The retained content can be reliably matched despite the expanded appendix in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original CQ-DINO experiments on V3Det and COCO, including detection results, component ablations, scalability measurements, and training-gradient analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds extended gradient measurements, isolated component ablations, and failure analyses in Appendices A.5, A.6, and A.8.

M1.justification: The main architecture, losses, and training procedure are retained. However, new Algorithm 3 computes the hierarchical weight as min(w+r,1), whereas Equation 7 in both versions uses w(1+r), with r the logarithmic child-count ratio. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedure change or a pseudocode error.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate V3Det and COCO with the same detection tasks. The added frequency and object-scale analyses subdivide existing V3Det evaluation data; they introduce no new dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged. Added analyses reuse CQ-DINO and existing DINO loss variants. Category-query methods newly discussed in Section 2.3 are cited predecessors, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Main benchmark settings remain unchanged, but substantial new evaluation designs appear: separate training and inference selection controls in Table 10, extended gradient tracking described through 400k iterations, hard negatives defined by the highest-scoring 10% of negative categories, and stratified evaluation of 3,527 categories below 83.3% recall.

E4.justification: Appendices A.5, A.6, and A.8 add extended gradient-ratio analyses, ablations isolating training versus inference selection, and failure analyses by category frequency and object scale. These substantially expand the examination of mechanisms and weaknesses. The earlier focal-loss and query-count studies are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v3, v4's checklist item 7 states that fixed seeds were used and results varied minimally across multiple random seeds. It explicitly reports no error bars or significance tests. Seed values, run counts, and numerical variability remain unspecified; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Headline benchmark results remain unchanged, including 53.0 AP on V3Det with Swin-L and 58.5 AP on COCO. New Table 10 reports V3Det results of 51.3 AP for training-only selection and 46.6 AP for inference-only selection with category correlations. Tables 12–13 add low-recall subset results, including 20.5 AP for rare categories and 14.1 AP for small objects; Figures 7–8 add gradient trajectories.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 generalizes the gradient-ratio argument using class sample counts and average positive and negative gradient magnitudes, culminating in Equation 8. This extends the mathematical treatment of vocabulary size versus class imbalance. The main-text derivations in Equations 1–7 are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain their substantive claims and reported performance advantage. Section 2.3 adds a qualified priority claim that the work provides the first systematic theoretical analysis of gradient dilution in vast-vocabulary settings.

C2.justification: New discussion distinguishes vocabulary-driven dilution from class imbalance, attributes accuracy benefits specifically to training-stage selection, and explains why inference-only filtering can hurt V3Det performance. Appendix A.8 additionally identifies rare categories and small objects as important failure conditions and interprets these difficulties as shared with DINO.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 supplies pseudocode for the three existing components, making tensor operations, normalization, and tree traversal more explicit. The stated repository location changes from RedAIGC/CQ-DINO to FireRedTeam/CQ-DINO, and the checklist adds supplemental-code availability statements. Main implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning around category-query predecessors, including Query2Label, ML-Decoder, CQL, ControlCap, and RankSeg. It acknowledges earlier category embeddings and top-k selection, then distinguishes CQ-DINO through gradient-dilution analysis and hierarchical category modeling.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include the new related-work subsection, updated author and affiliation information, conference front matter, acknowledgments, and a checklist. Existing appendix sections are preserved within the expanded A.1–A.8 organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 7–8, Tables 10, 12, and 13, and three algorithm displays. Figure 6 is redrawn with changed colors and legend placement and without the earlier scatter points. Existing figures and tables are reflowed, while v3's query-count Table 10 becomes Table 11.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's combined component ablations, v4's Table 10 better separates training benefits from inference filtering. Expanded gradient and failure analyses and discussion of category-query predecessors improve evidential support and positioning. These gains are tempered by the Equation 7/Algorithm 3 conflict, duplicated DINO labels in Table 12, and Figure 6 removing scatter points still invoked by its discussion.
